patterns: New model, mixed reviews: GPT-6.2 Astra launch dominated AI X. emollick 'very uneven & weird' (82.9K), Teknium's Blender before/after comparison (100.3K), emollick 'vibe benchmarks' (32.7K) and 'don't extrapolate from each new model' (20.5K); the hook is honest first-hand testing, not hype

Safe defaults and outages: levelsio asking VPS makers for a default firewall and Tailscale (180.3K, 1,437 bookmarks), SahilBloom 'are there more outages than normal?' (184.0K, top post), emollick on improvised infrastructure prone to cascading failures (38.2K); gregisenberg 'cybersecurity is the best business' twice (47.8K, 26.8K)

Open source and SaaS squeeze: gregisenberg 'make popular SaaS free and open source, upsell power users' (81.8K, 1,115 bookmarks); levelsio 'no real way to survive for most SaaS companies' (69.3K, 509 bookmarks)
Play and tinkering: levelsio on normies not understanding his for-fun projects (139.6K, 1,386 bookmarks) and his Feb 2025 couch Mario Kart attempt with Claude (104.6K)

Big numbered lists get saved: businessbarista '103 AI use cases that were impossible two years ago' (11.0K, 268 bookmarks); SahilBloom simple life advice on receiving a compliment (81.9K, 438 bookmarks)

narrative_synthesis: Tuesday into Wednesday was GPT-6.2 Astra day. Early testers were blunt: emollick called it very uneven and weird (82.9K) and Teknium's Blender before/after drew 100.3K. The most saved post was emollick on Anthropic's case for simple agents over a sprawl of subagents (168.8K, 1,972 saves). SahilBloom asked if outages are rising (184.0K, the top post), levelsio wanted VPS servers safe by default (180.3K, 1,437 saves), and gregisenberg kept pushing open-source SaaS and cybersecurity. In Indochina, Vietnam's central bank put limits and consent rules on AI-made payments, Vietnam launched an AI handbook for teachers, and Cambodia is building a national AI research centre with France.

indochina_ai.title: The State Bank of Vietnam's Circular 53/2026 on AI in banking is now in effect: AI-executed payments over VND10 million per transaction (VND20 million a day) for individuals count as high-risk, AI payments are capped at VND100 million a day per individual, customers must sign an agreement before AI can pay for them, and AI lending decisions of VND50 million or more need extra oversight

Vietnam's Ministry of Education and Training and RMIT University Vietnam launched an AI Handbook for Educators (with Aus4Skills support), six themes from basic AI literacy to lesson planning, assessment, learning resources, school admin and teachers' own growth, with human oversight and data privacy built in

At the close of FrancoTech 2026 in Phnom Penh (316 companies, 30,000+ registered participants), Cambodia's Ministry of Post and Telecommunications said it is working with France's AFD to set up a national AI and data science research centre, with about 10-20 preliminary cooperation agreements signed at the event
